alas! interjection

grief

also woe is me, ah me, woe, alack, woe to

classical

Plaut. Aul. 721: heu mē miserum, miserē periī

Heu!

alas! ah!

(Plaut., Ter.; Verg. and the poets)

The plain cry of grief or pain, often with the accusative of exclamation (heu mē miserum) or doubled.

Other words

  • Ēheu! — alas! ah!

    also used · classical · Hor. C. 2.14.1: ēheu fugācēs, Postume, Postume; Plaut. Capt. 995

    (Plaut., Ter.; Hor.)

    Lewis & Short: pain or grief, often with quam. It notes that many editors print heu heu for it in the poets.

  • Ei mihi! (Hei mihi!) — ah me! woe is me!

    also used · classical · Verg. A. 2.274: ei mihi, quālis erat; Ter. Ad. 323

    (Plaut., Ter.; Verg., Ov.)

    Lewis & Short (s.v. hei): grief or fear, “freq. joined with mihi”.

  • Vae …! — woe to …!

    with the dative (vae mihi, vae victīs), rarely the accusative · also used · classical · Plaut. Ps. 1317: Vae victīs.; Liv. 5.48.9

    Lewis & Short: “like the Gr. οὐαί and our woe!”. For the milder vae miserō mihi see oh dear!.

Examples

  • ēheu fugācēs, Postume, Postume, lābuntur annī

    alas, Postumus, Postumus, the fleeting years slip byHor. C. 2.14.1–2

  • ei mihi, quālis erat, quantum mūtātus ab illō

    ah me, how he looked! how changed from the man he wasVerg. A. 2.274

  • heu mē miserum, miserē periī

    alas, poor me, I’m wretchedly undonePlaut. Aul. 721

  • ēheu, quom ego plūs minusve fēcī quam mē aequom fuit.

    alas, that I did more or less than I should have!Plaut. Capt. 995

  • Vae victīs.

    Woe to the conquered.Plaut. Ps. 1317

See also oh dear!, ah!, damn!.
